subject: Clarify: streaming "stitching" charges, proration, and retries
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on how streaming is billed when clients disconnect/retry

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo today — the team liked how the streaming responses reduce perceived latency. Before we move forward with procurement we need a clear write-up on how Redwood bills for streaming output in a few edge cases:

- Partial generations: if the client disconnects mid-generation and the model emitted 30 tokens then the client reconnects and requests the remainder, do you bill for the 30 tokens plus the new ones emitted? Is there any stitching/proration?
- Retries: if our SDK retries automatically due to transient socket errors (i.e., client initiated reconnect within 10s), can we expect duplicated billing?
- Disconnect windows: do you have a grace window where you don’t bill repeated partials from the same session id?

We can provide logs and SDK behavior if that helps (attached a short snippet). Also include any recommended best practices (idempotency tokens, session ids) so our engineering team can implement properly.

Appended: acme_streaming_logs.txt (sample).

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Health
(attachment: acme_streaming_logs.txt)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on how streaming is billed when clients disconnect/retry

Maya — great to hear the demo landed. Short answer up front: we bill for tokens emitted by the model, but there are guardrails and recommended patterns that usually prevent double-billing for expected retry patterns. Below is an operational summary; I'll follow up with Marissa and Ben about offering a one-time goodwill credit while you test.

1) Billing granularity
- We meter on emitted output tokens (token-level). If the model emits 30 tokens before a disconnect, those 30 tokens are billable. If you subsequently re-request the same content and the model emits them again, those new emissions are also billable.

2) Stitching / proration
- We don’t currently have automatic "stitching" that marks a subsequent continuation as non-billable. Instead, we provide an optional session-id and idempotency token feature: if the SDK includes a session-id + resume-token, the service can detect continuation and avoid re-emitting tokens that were already acknowledged. This requires the client to surface the resume token on reconnect.

3) Grace window & retry behavior
- We support a configurable grace window (default 30s) where the reconnect with the same session-id and resume-token is treated as continuation, not a new generation. Retries outside that window are treated as a new request.
- For automatic SDK retries (transient network blips within the grace window) we recommend enabling the SDK’s built-in idempotency header so the server can correlate and suppress duplicate billing.

4) Practical guidance
- Use the streaming resume token returned by the SDK and pass it back on reconnect.
- If you can, signal whether the client consumed the last tokens (ack) — that makes suppression exact.
- For high-availability clients, combine a 30s grace window with an idempotency header tied to a user/request id.

I’m attaching a short draft breakdown of how charges would look across three scenarios (happy path, interrupted/resumed, retry-doubled). If that looks ok I’ll run it by Finance for a one-time test credit while Acme validates in staging.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_draft_billing_breakdown.pdf)

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on how streaming is billed when clients disconnect/retry

Thanks Vivek — that clarifies a lot. Couple of follow-ups and a concrete scenario:

Scenario: our mobile client begins a stream and receives 30 tokens, then the network drops and the client reconnects after 12s. The client currently calls your SDK restart routine without passing any resume token (old SDK behavior). In that case we expect to be billed for the new emissions as well, correct?

If Acme wants to avoid double-billing while we update the SDK across millions of devices, would Redwood consider:
- a temporary leniency window where repeated partial generations from the same account/session id within 60s are credited automatically?
- or a one-time pilot credit for invoices during our validation period?

We appreciate the session-id guidance — the engineering team will add resume tokens, but rolling that to clients will take time. Attached is an invoice snippet showing a few spikes we believe are caused by retries.

Regards,
Maya
(attachment: acme_invoice_snippet.png)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Questions on how streaming is billed when clients disconnect/retry

Marissa / Ben / Karthik — forwarding Acme’s ask. TL;DR: they need a short-term mitigation while they roll the resume-token update to mobile clients. They’ve provided logs and an invoice snippet showing spikes.

Proposal I think is reasonable: offer a one-time invoice credit for confirmed retry-induced spikes during the 30-day validation window, plus a temporary reduced streaming rate (10% discount) for the next 90 days if they commit to instrumenting resume tokens and a rollout plan. We should keep this narrowly scoped to their hosted API usage and require an engineering acceptance checklist.

Questions:
- Marissa: confirm approval authority for a one-time credit up to $15k for a strategic health-care account.
- Ben: can you draft the conditional credit terms (HubSpot line item + how we flag refunded tokens)?
- Karthik: please prepare the sales-side note for the quote / updated rate card; we’ll tie the discount to a three-month commit and an engineering acceptance form.

I’ll wait on your replies before sending the offer back to Maya.

Thanks,
Vivek

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on how streaming is billed when clients disconnect/retry

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear examples and attachments. We reviewed your logs and Vivek’s proposed approach and are happy to proceed with a pragmatic plan:

1) One-time invoice credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit up to $12,500 for confirmed retry-related token spikes in the invoice period ending 2027-04-30. To qualify we’ll need the Acme engineering acceptance checklist completed (we’ll share), and the logs showing correlation to identical user/session ids.

2) Temporary rate reduction: we’ll apply a 10% discount on streaming output tokens for your hosted API calls for 90 days from the start of the pilot (estimated start: 2027-04-15). This is conditional on a short rollout plan to adopt resume tokens and idempotency headers.

3) Implementation guidance:
- Use session-id + resume-token as Vivek outlined.
- If you can’t immediately push the SDK change to all clients, we recommend enabling a client-side debounce (500ms) to reduce spurious reconnects.

4) Next steps:
- I’ll upload the draft credit memo and quote to HubSpot and send a DocuSign for the pilot terms.
- Please complete the engineering acceptance checklist within 7 business days so Finance can validate the credit.

We’ll also add a short section to our public docs about recommended SDK config for streaming resumability (link). If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute technical working session next week to pair with your engineers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Director, Account Management
Redwood Inference
